h1: The 7 Best Cordless Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Cordless Leaf Blowers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 7 cordless leaf blowers from Milwaukee, Ryobi, DEWALT and value brands, compared on listed CFM, battery platform and price.
summary: The Milwaukee M18 FUEL is our top pick for a proven battery platform at 450 CFM. Ryobi ONE+ is the platform pick for existing owners, LOSART and YOOVL give 650 CFM on a budget, and MZK is the cheapest.
intro: The trap with cordless blowers is the number on the box. A 650 CFM claim from an unknown brand and a 450 CFM claim from a tool-platform brand are not the same promise.

We reviewed seven cordless blowers from the listings and ranked them on listed airflow, brand platform and price tier. Several budget models list higher CFM than the name brands, so we weighed that against support.

products.name: Milwaukee M18 FUEL 120 MPH 450 CFM 18-Volt Lithium Ion Brushless Blower
products.verdict: A brushless blower on the M18 platform.
products.description:
The Milwaukee M18 FUEL lists 120 MPH and 450 CFM from a brushless 18 volt motor, in the $100-200 tier.

It leads because it pairs solid airflow with a major tool platform. Budget models list more CFM, but none carries this support.

It suits owners of M18 batteries. The caveat is that it costs more than value brands.

products.name: RYOBI ONE+ 18V 100 MPH 325 CFM Cordless Battery Variable Speed Jet Fan Blower
products.verdict: Variable speed on the huge ONE+ battery system.
products.description:
Ryobi lists 100 MPH, 325 CFM and a variable speed trigger on the 18V ONE+ system, in the $100-200 tier.

It ranks second because its airflow is lower than Milwaukee and the value brands, but the ONE+ battery family is a big draw.

It suits owners of Ryobi tools. The caveat is the lower CFM.
cons: Lowest CFM of the big brands

products.name: LOSART Leaf Blower Cordless
products.verdict: A 650 CFM claim in the $50-100 tier.
products.description:
LOSART lists 650 CFM on battery power in the $50-100 tier.

It ranks third because the airflow beats the name brands on paper, but it lacks their platform and track record.

It suits budget buyers. The caveat is that CFM is a manufacturer claim.

products.name: YOOVL Leaf Blower Cordless
products.description:
YOOVL lists 650 CFM on battery power in the $50-100 tier.

It ranks fourth because it matches LOSART on paper and gives you no way to separate them on specs.

It suits budget buyers who find LOSART out of stock. The caveat is the same unproven track record.

products.name: MZK 20V Cordless Leaf Blower
products.verdict: 450 CFM in the lowest price tier here.
products.description:
MZK lists 450 CFM on a 20V battery in the $25-50 tier, the lowest in this ranking.

It ranks fifth because it undercuts everything on price while matching Milwaukee on listed CFM.

It suits small yards. The caveat is limited track record.

products.name: MTKOALA 2026 Upgrade Leaf Blower
products.verdict: 450 CFM at a slightly higher price than MZK.
products.description:
MTKOALA lists 450 CFM on battery power in the $50-100 tier.

It ranks sixth because MZK offers the same listed CFM for less.

It suits buyers who prefer its design. The caveat is that it costs more than MZK for the same claim.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX Blower
products.verdict: A compact 20V MAX blower for existing DEWALT batteries.
products.description:
DEWALT lists a 100 CFM output on the 20V MAX platform, in the $100-200 tier.

It ranks last because its airflow is the lowest here, but the DEWALT platform has value.

It suits owners of 20V MAX batteries doing light clean-up. The caveat is the airflow.

methodology.title: Listed airflow
methodology.description: CFM counted as a claim, not a measurement.

methodology.title: Battery platform
methodology.description: Major platforms scored higher for batteries and parts.

whatMatters.detail: CFM is how much air the blower moves each minute. Higher numbers clear leaves faster. Look for the CFM number in the title and compare it only against similar brands.
MPH is how fast the air leaves the nozzle, which helps lift wet or stuck leaves. A listing with only CFM tells half the story. Look for both numbers.
Buying into a platform means batteries swap across tools. If you own M18, ONE+ or 20V MAX, buy that. Check whether the battery is included.
A brushless motor tends to run cooler and last longer than a brushed one. Look for the word brushless in the bullets.
Batteries age. A known brand makes replacement packs easier to buy. Check the listed warranty.

finalTake: The Milwaukee M18 FUEL is our top pick for platform and support. Ryobi suits ONE+ owners, LOSART is the value airflow pick, and MZK is the cheapest. Pick by battery first.
